CAPIOX Hemoconcentrators are used during cardiopulmonary bypass to remove excess fluid from blood, maintain proper hematocrit and protein concentration, and enable reinfusion of blood remaining in the circuit after bypass. Their polysulfone membrane is designed to achieve a high ultrafiltration rate (UFR), concentrating blood efficiently in a short time while restricting albumin removal. The inlet blood port is designed to support smooth flow, reduce possible stagnation, and prevent thrombus formation. Low-priming-volume filters are intended to keep the device compact and light, require little storage space, and allow easy disposal. No-rinse hollow fibers are designed for quick setup, including during an operation. The transparent housing, including blood ports, is designed to allow visual checking.

Immunoassay Systems are analyzers that use antibodies or antigens to measure molecule concentrations for diagnostic purposes using test cartridges. Detection methods can include enzymes, radioactive isotopes, DNA probes, fluorescence, and electrochemiluminescence. Depending on the device, test modes can include read now and walk away modes.

For medical product descriptions, the user wants the product profile to follow the product description manual and the style of the examples: concise, factual paragraphs that introduce the product and intended use, then explain components, technologies, workflow, and specific features. State claims with wording such as “designed to” or “intended to” when appropriate; avoid unsupported claims and do not repeat features already explained. The user sometimes specifies an exact word count and requests an unbiased description containing all supplied facts.

The user provided a VITROS 3600 Immunodiagnostic System profile as a style example: it describes quantitative, semi-quantitative, and qualitative assay measurements; MicroWell, Intellicheck, and MicroSensor technologies; intended operating-efficiency and turnaround-time benefits; standardization with other VITROS systems; changing consumables, waste, and reagents during operation for uninterrupted workflow; and ease of use and environmental considerations.

The user provided a VITROS 4600 profile as a style example. It describes in vitro measurement of clinical analytes in serum, plasma, urine, and cerebrospinal fluid; components including a clinical chemistry analyzer, display monitor, controls, reagents, and disposable instrumentation; VITROS MicroSlide technology intended to minimize operator interventions and maximize ease of use; and VITROS Intellicheck technology designed for real-time process monitoring and reducing the risk of incorrect result reporting.

The user provided the Sofia Fluorescent Immunoassay Analyzer profile as a style example. It describes a benchtop analyzer for fluorescent detection of pathogens, using an ultraviolet LED source and sensor to collect data from test cassettes. Separately purchased tests include hCG, Influenza A and B, RSV, and Strep A. Walk-away mode develops and scans a single-patient sample cassette in the analyzer; read-now mode allows the user to develop samples outside the analyzer before insertion and immediate scanning. Results display within one minute. The analyzer has an integrated printer, and results can be printed, stored on the supplied SD card, or sent to a laboratory information system (LIS).
